subject: Pelican2b elevated 5xx/timeouts — triage & customer update
messages:
From: Ethan Browne <ethan@pureanalytics.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 07 Jun 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike of 500s / timeouts on Pelican2b since 14:30 PT

Hi Rafael,

We're seeing a spike of 500 responses and several long-running timeouts from calls routed to model 'pelican2b' starting ~14:30 PT today. Impact is primarily our chat summarization endpoint (short prompts, 256 token context). Error rate climbed from ~0.5% to ~8% over 20 minutes. We captured a few request IDs and a sample log — attaching one.

Sample symptomatic behavior: repeated 5xx with message "inference_failed: kernel timeout" and a few requests that hang >30s then fail. Our platform is in us-west region and we saw retries from worker pool. Can you confirm if Redwood is seeing a model-side issue or if this is on our side? We're currently throttling traffic to reduce customer impact but would like to know estimated ETA for recovery.

I've copied Olivia (platform lead) in case we need a phone bridge.

Thanks,
Ethan Browne
SRE Lead, Pure Analytics

Attachment: pelican-sample-500.log (text/plain)

Subject: Re: Spike of 500s / timeouts on Pelican2b since 14:30 PT

Quick triage notes (what we observed):

Timeline
- 14:27 PT: increased queuing observed on pelican2b GPU pools in us-west-2.
- 14:30 PT: kernel-level timeouts start surfacing; majority of failures are 'kernel execution exceeded allowed time' from reclaimed preempted kernels.
- 14:35 PT: autoscaler attempted to add capacity but hit pod scheduling pressure on a subset of hosts (driver-side driver bug with newer AMI).

Root cause (prelim)
- A recent kernel selection change for pelican2b (deployed 06-07-2028 13:50 PT) introduced a regression under short-sequence, high-concurrency workloads — it selects a fast-path kernel that does not properly handle an edge-case for our memory allocator leading to transient stalls and subsequent kernel timeouts.

Actions taken (in-flight)
- Rolled back kernel selection to previous stable profile for pelican2b in us-west-2 (completed 15:30 PT) — this should eliminate the regression.
- Temporarily pinned affected customers' routes to pelican2b-variant-stable where available.
- Enabled an emergency circuit-breaker for long-running inference requests in the gateway to fail fast after 5s and trigger fallback to pelican2b-lite.
- Created INFRA-9821 to track remediation and root cause patching (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-9821).

Observed effect
- Error rate started decreasing after the rollback; by 15:50 PT error rate down to ~1.2%. We continue to monitor token-level failures and latency p50/p99.

Next steps
- Full patch to kernel selector scheduled for 06-08-2028 04:00 PT in a controlled rollout (can accelerate if needed).
- Postmortem with affected teams tomorrow; will include deeper allocator trace and reproducer.
- We'll share an incident timeline and mitigation verification report with Pure Analytics within 48 hours.

Attachments: INFRA-9821-triage-notes.pdf, pelican-p50-p99-dashboard.png

Markus Klein
Senior Infra Engineer, Runtime Reliability | markus@redwood.com

Subject: Pelican2b — recovery confirmation and follow-up meeting

Hi Ethan / Olivia —

Thanks again for flagging the spike and for your patience while our team triaged. Quick summary for Pure Analytics: 

What happened
- A recent runtime kernel selection change caused transient kernel timeouts under your workload profile (short prompts, high concurrency).

What we did for you
- Immediately rolled back the kernel selector for Pelican2b in us-west and pinned your production routes to the stable variant until the patch is verified.
- Enabled gateway circuit-breaker and fallback to pelican2b-lite for long requests, which prevented further customer-facing outages.
- Provided a sample of the logs you sent to the infra team for correlation.

Current state
- Traffic for your account routed normally since ~15:55 PT on 06-07-2028; we've seen error rates return to baseline and p99 latency improving. We'll continue 72-hour elevated monitoring.

Follow-up
- We've scheduled a brief post-incident walkthrough with infra and SRE tomorrow 06-10-2028 09:00 PT to review timeline, mitigations, and planned patch (30 minutes). Meeting invite: https://calendar.redwood.com/meet/incident-pelican2b-pureanalytics
- We'll deliver a written postmortem and verification artifacts (traces, reproducer) within 48 hours.

Credits/commitment
- Monica will follow up on any SLA credit or one-time make-good per your contract.

If you'd like an immediate bridge for deeper log correlation, let me know and we'll open one.
